ownership_summary: Listed on Boursa Kuwait. Per Boursa Kuwait data at 19 Jul 2026 (H1 2026 investor presentation): Public Institution for Social Security 11.7%, Behbehani Investment Co. 9.9%, Behbehani General Trading Co. 9.5%, Ali Morad Yousuf Behbehani 6.9%, Behbehani Financial Co. 5.0%, free float below 5% 57.1%. The four holders carrying the Behbehani name together hold 31.3% on these figures; the bank says it has retained the same core shareholder base since 1967.
government_link: Partial - the Public Institution for Social Security (a Kuwaiti public institution) holds 11.7% (Boursa Kuwait data, 19 Jul 2026); no controlling government holding.
group_structure: Subsidiaries (31 Dec 2025): Ahli Capital Investment Company K.S.C.(C) 99.8% (investment arm trading as ABK Wealth Management, with ABK Wealth Management DIFC / ABK Capital DIFC Ltd est. 2025); Al Ahli Bank of Kuwait - Egypt S.A.E. 98.7% (ABK-Egypt, acquired Nov 2015; 47 branches) with its Leasing (98.6%) and Investment (98.7%) companies; ABK Cayman Island Limited 100%. UAE operations are branches of the bank (Dubai, Abu Dhabi, DIFC). ABK Wealth Management and ABK-Egypt are not profiled separately, so their details are recorded here; ABK-Egypt is consolidated in the group figures.

capabilities.wealth_summary: ABK has made wealth an explicit growth pillar: in 2025 it merged Private Banking with its CMA-licensed investment arm Ahli Capital Investment Company (99.8% owned, est. 2006) into ABK Wealth Management, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer and run by CEO Sherif ElRafie, and set up ABK Wealth Management DIFC (DFSA Category 3C). Offers include discretionary portfolios (Conservative, Moderate, Growth by target volatility), a fund range (Al Ahli Kuwaiti Fund, Al Ahli Gulf Fund, KD and USD money market funds, and the BlackRock-sub-managed Ahli International Multi-Asset Holding Fund), private markets (infrastructure and private equity solutions launched 2025; Barings KD-denominated private credit, June 2026; partnerships with BlackRock and Blackstone), investment advisory, investment banking and the ABK Wealth Trade brokerage covering Kuwait, GCC, Egypt and US markets. ABK says its wealth client base grew about 50% and discretionary AUM about 30% year on year at H1 2026 but publishes no AUM amount. A flagship 'Digital Investment Access Platform' was in development per AR 2025, and a new group strategy is being finalised as the five-year plan to 2026 ends.

private_banking.detail: Private Banking is delivered by the bank and branded ABK Wealth Management since 2025: dedicated branches, committed relationship manager, preferential rates, loans against multiple asset types, UAE mortgage, private credit card, family banking packages, concierge and invite-only events. Ahli Capital itself provides no banking services (disclaimer on S17). Private banking rebranded from 'Private Banking' with ABK Capital in 2025 (AR 2025).

asset_management.detail: Ahli Capital Investment Company K.S.C.(C) (99.8% ABK, est. 2006, CMA-regulated) trading as ABK Wealth Management: funds, discretionary portfolios, private credit, private equity, real estate, leasing and asset-backed finance. Funds: Al Ahli Kuwaiti Fund (Feb 2003), Al Ahli Gulf Fund (Aug 2003; SICO Bahrain sub-manager for non-Kuwait allocation), Ahli Capital KD Money Market Fund, Ahli Capital USD Money Market Fund (subscription period extended Feb and Apr 2026), Ahli International Multi-Asset Holding Fund (Nov 2018). ABK Wealth Management DIFC (DFSA Category 3C): managing assets, arranging deals, advising, custody. AUM amount not disclosed.

brokerage.detail: ABK Wealth Trade: one account for Kuwait, GCC, Egypt and US markets; stocks, ETFs and bonds/sukuk; online platform (phone, desktop), direct broker access; iOS and Android apps; account funding through ABK Mobile Banking. The platform login is hosted at abk.globaltradingnetwork.com (vendor inferred from the domain). Online brokerage platform rolled out in 2025 (AR 2025).

digital_investing.detail: ABK Wealth Trade app and client portal; funding of brokerage accounts through ABK Mobile Banking; 'Digital Investment Access Platform' (single digital gateway to all investment offerings) was being built in 2025 (AR 2025); new ABK mobile app serves Mass, Elite and Private segments (4.7 app-store rating).

advisory.detail: Investment advisory for HNW individuals, affluent retail clients and corporates; investment banking team advised on the bank's Tier 2 issuance and a Markaz bond in 2025.

discretionary.detail: Ahli Capital offers 'tailored discretionary portfolio management' (public markets multi-asset income portfolios with Conservative 5-8%, Moderate 5-10% and Growth above 10% target volatility; private markets). Discretionary AUM grew about 30% year on year at H1 2026 (no amount).

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Model and custom portfolios by volatility band under discretionary management (S11); no retail robo-advisor found.

funds_platform.detail: Own and third-party-managed funds: BlackRock Investment Management (UK) sub-manages the Ahli International Multi-Asset Holding Fund (fund of funds, KD 500 minimum, 1.35% management fee, monthly dealing); SICO sub-manages the non-Kuwait allocation of Al Ahli Gulf Fund; partnerships with Barings and Blackstone. Platform provider not named.

structured_products.detail: 'Structured Products' is listed under ABK Wealth Management's products and services on its homepage; no detail page was read, and the bank's AR also cites access to 'structured solutions'.

private_markets.detail: New infrastructure and private equity investment solutions launched in 2025; Barings partnership for KD-denominated global private credit (24 Jun 2026); private credit, private equity, real estate, leasing and asset-backed finance offered through Ahli Capital.

islamic_wealth.detail: ABK is a conventional bank; no Shariah-compliant funds or portfolios found on the wealth pages read.

initiatives.what: Launched ABK Wealth Management by merging Private Banking and ABK Capital (Ahli Capital); established ABK Capital DIFC (DFSA Category 3C); launched infrastructure and private equity solutions; rolled out online brokerage; started the Digital Investment Access Platform; first NexGen client programme (Geneva).
Giel-Jan Van Der Tol became Group CEO (appointment reported July 2025).
Issued KD 30 million Tier II bond, significantly oversubscribed.
Initial subscription period for the Ahli Capital USD Money Market Fund extended; closing date later moved again on 27 Apr 2026.

opportunities: Wealth is a stated priority: Kuwait strategy to 'scale franchise in retail, private banking, and commercial banking' (S6 p.16); ABK Wealth Management launched 2025; retail growth directed at affluent, HNW and youth (S5 p.15).
Flagship 'Digital Investment Access Platform', a single gateway to all investment offerings, was being built in 2025 with no vendor named (S5 p.31).

Wealth momentum with no amounts disclosed: client base up about 50% and discretionary AUM up about 30% year on year (S7 p.7); new strategy cycle being finalised and digital CAPEX, Open Banking and AI cited (S7 p.8).
Affluent tier (Elite / Elite Plus packages) shows no investing proposition on the retail pages read; model portfolios are offered only through Ahli Capital's discretionary service (S11).
barriers: Established in-house asset manager (Ahli Capital) with named global partners: BlackRock, Blackstone, Barings and SICO (S5, S13, S19).
Brokerage already runs on a dedicated platform (domain suggests Global Trading Network) and Digital Investment Access Platform work is under way (S9, S5).
Conventional-only bank: no Islamic wealth shelf found (S9, S13).
Group in leadership transition: new Group CEO from July 2025 and a Kuwait CEO still acting (S1, S5).
